sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In 2005, I took a job at WBEZ in Chicago, and I was so excited to be moving there.
sentences.zh: 2005年，我在芝加哥的WBEZ电台找到了一份工作，当时我非常兴奋能搬到那里去。

sentences.en: I was excited about the job, of course, but I was also very excited about the grid.
sentences.zh: 当然，我为这份工作感到兴奋，但我更兴奋的是那里的网格系统。

sentences.en: The streets of Chicago and the address numbering system are beautiful.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥的街道和门牌编号系统非常美妙。

sentences.en: Starting from the 00 access point downtown, the streets conform to a rigid grid pattern
sentences.zh: 从市中心的00坐标点开始，街道遵循着严格的网格模式，

sentences.en: where the major streets are exactly one mile apart and have address numbers which are in multiples of 800.
sentences.zh: 主要街道之间正好相隔一英里，门牌号以800为倍数递增。

sentences.en: You don't really have to be able to picture this, but I know that if you know it,
sentences.zh: 你其实不需要在脑海中构想出这个画面，但我知道如果你了解它，

sentences.en: you're nodding your head vigorously, but just know that it's amazing, and I was mesmerized by it.
sentences.zh: 你现在一定在用力点头，它真的很神奇，我当时完全被它迷住了。

sentences.en: So much so that I made flashcards with Chicago street names on one side
sentences.zh: 以至于我制作了抽认卡，一面写着芝加哥的街道名称，

sentences.en: and the corresponding address number on the other
sentences.zh: 另一面写着对应的门牌号，

sentences.en: so that my wife and I could quiz ourselves on the 2,000-mile road trip from San Francisco to Chicago.
sentences.zh: 这样我和我妻子就能在从旧金山到芝加哥那2000英里的公路旅行中互相测试。

sentences.en: Yes, I was always like this.
sentences.zh: 没错，我一直都是这样的人。

sentences.en: Division is 1,200 north.
sentences.zh: 迪维申街（Division）是北纬1200号。

sentences.en: Armitage is 2,000 north, and therefore one mile north of Division.
sentences.zh: 阿米蒂奇街（Armitage）是北纬2000号，也就是在迪维申街以北一英里的地方。

sentences.en: After living in the jumble of San Francisco streets for years,
sentences.zh: 在旧金山那种杂乱无章的街道上生活了多年之后，

sentences.en: the thought of moving to a place where people planned the city to help people know where they were
sentences.zh: 想到要搬到一个人们为了帮助他人辨别方位而规划城市的地方，

sentences.en: and where they were going soothed my lizard brain and gave me peace.
sentences.zh: 想到要去往哪里，这安抚了我原始的大脑，让我感到平静。

sentences.en: As humans have developed cities and built environments,
sentences.zh: 随着人类开发城市和建造环境，

sentences.en: we have also needed to develop ways to find our way through them.
sentences.zh: 我们也需要开发出在其中找到方向的方法。

sentences.en: Signage goes back at least as far as the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 导视系统至少可以追溯到罗马帝国时期。

sentences.en: They constructed milestones along their roadways.
sentences.zh: 他们在道路沿线建造了里程碑。

sentences.en: Which is to say, if you're relying on anything besides natural features to help you find your way around,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，如果你除了自然地标之外，还要依靠其他东西来帮你辨别方向，

sentences.en: you are relying on things made by people whose job it is,
sentences.zh: 那你就是在依靠那些以帮助我们从各自的A点到达B点为职业的人所创造的东西。

sentences.en: is to help us figure out how to get from all of our respective point A's to our point B's.
sentences.zh: 我们的制作人萨姆·格林斯潘想让我告诉你，他的方向感好得惊人。

sentences.en: Our producer Sam Greenspan would like me to tell you that he has a fantastic sense of direction.
sentences.zh: 我确实很好。

sentences.en: I really do.
sentences.zh: 当然，我承认有时候也会迷路。

sentences.en: Sure, I get lost sometimes, I'll admit it.
sentences.zh: 那感觉糟透了。

sentences.en: It's the worSt.
sentences.zh: 发生这种情况时，我对自己非常生气。

sentences.en: I get so mad at myself when it happens.
sentences.zh: 但现在，自从我开始思考“寻路系统”这一概念的意义后，我的生活完全不同了。

sentences.en: But now, my life is completely different ever since I started thinking about what it means that wayfinding is a thing.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，寻路系统是环境图形设计的一个分支，旨在帮助人们找到方向。

sentences.en: Wayfinding, in this sense, is a branch of environmental graphic design concerned with helping people find their way.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢了解这一点，因为现在，当我在医院、复杂的立交桥或机场迷路时，

sentences.en: I love knowing this, because now, when I get lost in a hospital, or in a complicated freeway interchange, or at an airport,
sentences.zh: 我终于有可以责怪的对象了。

sentences.en: I have someone to blame.
sentences.zh: 没错，这确实是一种看待问题的方式。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's one way to look at it.
sentences.zh: 但很多时候，这与导视牌无关。

sentences.en: But a lot of times it has nothing to do with the signage.
sentences.zh: 有时候确实是用户自己的错。

sentences.en: User error does apply sometimes.
sentences.zh: 说得有道理。

sentences.en: Fair enough.
sentences.zh: 让我为你介绍一下吉姆·哈丁。

sentences.en: Let me introduce you to Jim Harding.
sentences.zh: 我叫吉姆·哈丁。

sentences.en: My name is Jim Harding.
sentences.zh: 我是一名环境图形设计师。

sentences.en: I'm an environmental graphic designer.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，我负责告诉人们该往哪走。

sentences.en: Basically, I tell people where to go.
sentences.zh: 每一块导视牌背后，都有一位环境图形设计师、寻路专家，或者可能只是一个拿着记号笔的孩子。

sentences.en: There's an environmental graphic designer, or wayfinder, or maybe just a kid with a magic marker, behind every sign.
sentences.zh: 在这里转弯汇入101号公路。

sentences.en: Turn here to merge onto the 101.
sentences.zh: C大厅往这边走。

sentences.en: Concourse C is this way.
sentences.zh: 洗手间就在前方。

sentences.en: Bathrooms straight ahead.
sentences.zh: 但寻路系统远不止导视牌那么简单。

sentences.en: But there is a lot, lot more to wayfinding than just signage.
sentences.zh: 导视牌可能是寻路系统中最不有效的工具。

sentences.en: Signage is probably the least effective tool of wayfinding.
sentences.zh: 优秀的建筑设计才是最好的工具之一。

sentences.en: Good architecture is one of the beSt.
sentences.zh: 并不是吉姆讨厌导视牌。

sentences.en: It's not that Jim hates signs.
sentences.zh: 而是说，最好的寻路形式是，我们姑且称之为“隐形”的。

sentences.en: Rather, the best forms of wayfinding are, shall we say, invisible.
sentences.zh: 它们融入了建筑环境之中。

sentences.en: They're baked into the built environment.
sentences.zh: 我最初是通过一位名叫大卫·茨威格的作家听说吉姆·哈丁的。

sentences.en: I first heard about Jim Harding through a writer named David Zweig.
sentences.zh: 我是大卫·茨威格。

sentences.en: I'm David Zweig.
sentences.zh: 我是一名作家。

sentences.en: I'm a writer.
sentences.zh: 我的书叫《隐形人：在无休止的自我推销时代，匿名工作的力量》。

sentences.en: My book is called Invisibles, The Power of Anonymous Work in an Age of Relentless Self-Promotion.
sentences.zh: 大卫·茨威格的书描绘了一系列他称之为“隐形人”的人。

sentences.en: David Zweig's book is a series of portraits of people whom he refers to as invisibles.
sentences.zh: 隐形人是指那些技术精湛的专业人士，

sentences.en: Invisibles are people who are highly skilled professionals,
sentences.zh: 他们对所参与的任何企业或事业都至关重要，

sentences.en: people who are really important to whatever enterprise or endeavor that they're a part of,
sentences.zh: 他们的工作对最终结果有着巨大的影响，

sentences.en: that their work really has a big effect on the overall outcome,
sentences.zh: 但他们却鲜为人知，从未被公众或终端用户所关注。

sentences.en: but yet who are largely unknown, never thought of by the public or the end user.
sentences.zh: 吉姆·哈丁，格雷沙姆·史密斯合伙人公司的环境图形总监，就是这样一位隐形人。

sentences.en: Jim Harding, director of environmental graphics for Gresham Smith & Partners, is one such invisible.
sentences.zh: 吉姆·哈丁是业内最顶尖的人才之一。

sentences.en: Jim Harding is one of the best in the business.
sentences.zh: 吉姆参与了佐治亚州亚特兰大哈茨菲尔德-杰克逊国际机场新国际航站楼的设计，

sentences.en: Jim worked on the new international terminal at Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport in Atlanta, Georgia,
sentences.zh: 那是世界上最繁忙的机场。

sentences.en: the world's busieSt.
sentences.zh: 每年有1亿名乘客穿梭其中，

sentences.en: 100 million passengers move through it every year,
sentences.zh: 他们都需要知道该往哪里走。

sentences.en: all of them needing to know where to go.
sentences.zh: 视线非常重要，因为如果你能看到目的地，就不需要依赖导视牌了。

sentences.en: Sightlines are so important, because if you can see your destination, you don't have to rely on signs.
sentences.zh: 我在亚特兰大机场见到了吉姆，

sentences.en: I met Jim at the Atlanta airport,
sentences.zh: 他带我参观了一些他在新国际航站楼采用的尖端寻路技术。

sentences.en: and he walked me through some of the cutting-edge wayfinding techniques
sentences.zh: 比如当你从路边走进来时，

sentences.en: that he employed at the new international terminal.
sentences.zh: 物理空间会告诉你所有需要知道的移动方式，

sentences.en: Like right when you walk in from curbside,
sentences.zh: 而你甚至都没有意识到这一点。

sentences.en: the physical space tells you everything you need to know about how to move through it,
sentences.zh: 让我们从进入机场后最先寻找的地方开始：值机柜台。

sentences.en: without you even realizing it.
sentences.zh: 它们不是排成90度直角的。

sentences.en: Let's start at the first thing you want when you enter the airport, the ticket counter.
sentences.zh: 它们是倾斜的，明白吗？

sentences.en: They're not lined up on a 90-degree axis.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，当你走进来时，值机柜台直接迎面而来，

sentences.en: They're angled, okay?
sentences.zh: 然后你就会纳闷：我是该往左走还是往右走？

sentences.en: A lot of times the ticket counter just meets you head-on when you walk in,
sentences.zh: 我的登机口指示牌在哪里？

sentences.en: and then you're left to wonder, okay, do I go left or right?
sentences.zh: 但这些倾斜的值机柜台会微妙地引导你朝正确的方向前进。

sentences.en: Where's the sign for my gate?
sentences.zh: 那个角度引导你绕过值机柜台，

sentences.en: But these angled ticket counters subtly push you in the right direction.
sentences.zh: 并朝安检口走去。

sentences.en: That angle steers you down and around the ticket counter
sentences.zh: 当柜台在推着你走的时候，

sentences.en: and heading toward the security checkpoint.
sentences.zh: 你同时也被这扇巨大的三层楼高的玻璃窗吸引，

sentences.en: As the counter is pushing you,
sentences.zh: 它正对着停机坪。

sentences.en: you're also getting pulled by this giant three-story glass window
sentences.zh: 你能看到飞机。

sentences.en: that looks out onto the tarmac.
sentences.zh: 你能看到停机坪、登机廊桥，以及飞机停靠的地方。

sentences.en: You see planes.
sentences.zh: 所以直觉上，你会被吸引向你的飞机，

sentences.en: You see the apron, the jetway, where the planes are parking.
sentences.zh: 因为那是你想去的地方。

sentences.en: And so intuitively, you're drawn to your plane
sentences.zh: 你想登上那架飞机，对吧？

sentences.en: because that's what you want to go.
sentences.zh: 而且还有一些不那么明显的线索，

sentences.en: You want to get on that plane, right?
sentences.zh: 比如地板上的瓷砖图案。

sentences.en: And there are less obvious cues, too,
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: like the tile pattern in the floor.
sentences.zh: 当你看到网格时，

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 它不是90度轴线的，

sentences.en: When you see the grid,
sentences.zh: 而是45度的。

sentences.en: instead of being on a 90-degree axis,
sentences.zh: 这些以45度角延伸的瓷砖，

sentences.en: it's on a 45.
sentences.zh: 它们仿佛在召唤你跟随它们。

sentences.en: And these tiles going off at a 45-degree angle,
sentences.zh: 如果你照做了，

sentences.en: they just beckon you to follow them.
sentences.zh: 你就会不可避免地走向安检处。

sentences.en: And so if you do that,
sentences.zh: 但地板上还有更多玄机。

sentences.en: you inevitably head toward security.
sentences.zh: 接下来这点会让你觉得有点疯狂。

sentences.en: But there's even more going on in the floor than that.
sentences.zh: 如果你转过身往回看，萨姆，

sentences.en: And here's where this gets a little bananas.
sentences.zh: 你看从路边入口处开始的黑色部分。

sentences.en: If you turn around and look back here, Sam,
sentences.zh: 在主网格图案中还有另一组瓷砖，

sentences.en: you see where the black starts at the door from the curbside.
sentences.zh: 我起初甚至都没注意到。

sentences.en: There's another set of tiles inside the dominant grid pattern
sentences.zh: 它从黑色开始，

sentences.en: that I didn't even notice at firSt.
sentences.zh: 然后加入了一组黄褐色的瓷砖，

sentences.en: It starts black,
sentences.zh: 它们勾勒出了一条负空间的走廊，

sentences.en: and then it's joined by a set of yellow goldish tiles
sentences.zh: 直接穿过大厅，

sentences.en: that kind of cleaves out this corridor of negative space,
sentences.zh: 直通安检处。

sentences.en: which cuts straight through the hall,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果我已经拿到了登机牌，

sentences.en: going directly to security.
sentences.zh: 不需要托运行李，

sentences.en: So, you know, if I already have my ticket,
sentences.zh: 也不需要去柜台办理值机，

sentences.en: I'm not checking any bags.
sentences.zh: 我就顺着这条“黄砖路”走就行了。

sentences.en: I don't need to, you know, check in on the counter.
sentences.zh: 顺着黄砖路走。

sentences.en: I just follow the yellow brick road, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: Follow the yellow brick road.
sentences.zh: 确实就是这样。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 这就是黄砖路。

sentences.en: That's exactly what it is.
sentences.zh: 这正是它的用意。

sentences.en: It's the yellow brick road.
sentences.zh: 就像灯泡突然亮了。

sentences.en: That's exactly what this is.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The little light bulb.
sentences.zh: 你终于明白了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 这太酷了。

sentences.en: It's clicking on you.
sentences.zh: 吉姆说，这一切都是100%刻意设计的。

sentences.en: It's pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And all this, Jim says, is 100% intentional.
sentences.zh: 我们的室内设计师尝试了多种地板图案设计方案，

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 才最终确定了这一种。

sentences.en: Our interior designers went through a number of flooring pattern design schemes
sentences.zh: 穿过安检后，我们进入了吉姆·哈丁所说的“过渡大厅”。

sentences.en: until we arrived at this one.
sentences.zh: 在这里，旅客需要做一些决定，

sentences.en: On the other side of security, we enter what Jim Harding calls the transition hall.
sentences.zh: 是去寻找登机口，还是去往另一个航站楼，

sentences.en: Here's where a traveler has some decisions to make,
sentences.zh: 你需要乘坐名为“飞机列车”的地铁去那里，

sentences.en: whether to find a gate here or whether to get to another concourse,
sentences.zh: 或者去行李提取处。

sentences.en: you take a subway called the plane train for that,
sentences.zh: 这是乘客们会问自己的地方：

sentences.en: or whether to head to baggage claim.
sentences.zh: 我在哪？

sentences.en: This is the part where passengers are going to be asking themselves,
sentences.zh: 我要去哪？

sentences.en: Where am I?
sentences.zh: 我怎么知道去那里的最佳路径？

sentences.en: Where am I going?
sentences.zh: 吉姆说，在这些需要做决定的地方，

sentences.en: How do I know the best way to get there?
sentences.zh: 正是最需要寻路系统的地方。

sentences.en: Jim says that in these places, where there are decisions to be made,
sentences.zh: 没错，视觉寻路系统，也就是导视牌。

sentences.en: this is where wayfinding is needed the moSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可以看到它，读懂它，解读它，从而找到方向。

sentences.en: Yeah, the visual wayfinding, which is the signage.
sentences.zh: 这里还有一个问讯处和一种新式的交互式显示屏。

sentences.en: You know, you can see it, you can read it, you can interpret it, find your way around.
sentences.zh: 我和吉姆一起走向登机口。

sentences.en: There's also an information desk and a newfangled interactive display.
sentences.zh: 这是F7，F9。

sentences.en: I walk with Jim towards the gates.
sentences.zh: 看来单数在左边。

sentences.en: Here's F7, F9.
sentences.zh: 非常好。

sentences.en: So it looks like the odds are on the left.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Very good.
sentences.zh: 你已经进入寻路状态了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 这个大厅非常简洁，甚至可以说很优雅。

sentences.en: You're into the wayfinding scene there.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This concourse is pretty streamlined, elegant even.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But at older, less well-designed concourses,
sentences.zh: 但在那些年代较久、设计欠佳的候机厅，

sentences.en: which are definitely present at some other parts of the ATL airport,
sentences.zh: 也就是亚特兰大机场其他区域确实存在的那种，

sentences.en: this is where you'd find yourself in a visual morass.
sentences.zh: 你就会发现自己陷入了一片视觉混乱之中。

sentences.en: You've seen this before.
sentences.zh: 这种场景你一定见过。

sentences.en: Neon signs and brightly colored displays,
sentences.zh: 霓虹灯招牌和色彩鲜艳的展示牌，

sentences.en: all trying to get you to buy magazines or neck pillows or hot dogs.
sentences.zh: 都在极力诱导你购买杂志、颈枕或热狗。

sentences.en: You have advertising, you have concessions, marketing,
sentences.zh: 广告、特许经营店、营销推广，

sentences.en: all those visual elements compete with the primary message of just how to navigate the airport.
sentences.zh: 所有这些视觉元素都在与机场最核心的导航信息争夺你的注意力。

sentences.en: And so the key here is to make the signage stand out by being dull and drab and plain.
sentences.zh: 所以这里的关键在于，要让导视系统通过平淡、枯燥和简洁的设计脱颖而出。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's very neutral.
sentences.zh: 没错，它非常中性。

sentences.en: It's a neutral palette, gray and white, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是一种灰白色的中性色调。

sentences.en: So you can spot the signs just by tuning out all the glitz.
sentences.zh: 这样你就能屏蔽掉所有浮夸的干扰，一眼看到导视牌。

sentences.en: Now, even though this new international terminal is fairly minimal,
sentences.zh: 虽然这个新的国际航站楼设计相当简约，

sentences.en: there are still people trying to sell you stuff.
sentences.zh: 但依然有人试图向你推销商品。

sentences.en: Just beyond the transition hall towards the gates, there's this two-level commerce area.
sentences.zh: 在穿过过渡大厅前往登机口的路上，有一个双层的商业区。

sentences.en: There's shopping at ground level and then up an escalator are some food options.
sentences.zh: 底层是购物区，乘自动扶梯上去还有一些餐饮选择。

sentences.en: And of course, it's all angled perfectly,
sentences.zh: 当然，这一切的角度都经过精心计算，

sentences.en: so you have a direct line of sight into all the shops as you're walking by.
sentences.zh: 让你在走过时能直接看到所有的商店。

sentences.en: Is that an intentional design, to have the shopping down below and the food up above?
sentences.zh: 将购物区设在下方，餐饮区设在上方，这是刻意的设计吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 为什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, more curb appeal for your retail tenants.
sentences.zh: 嗯，为了给零售租户增加吸引力。

sentences.en: People, if they're hungry, they're going to go find the food wherever it is, right?
sentences.zh: 人们如果饿了，无论食物在哪里，他们都会去找，对吧？

sentences.en: Here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 关键就在这里。

sentences.en: Airports, they struggle to generate revenue.
sentences.zh: 机场一直在为增加收入而苦恼。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so anything they can do to help increase non-aeronautical revenue,
sentences.zh: 所以他们会尽一切可能增加非航空收入，

sentences.en: things that are not generated by a plane or an airline.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些并非由飞机或航空公司直接产生的收入。

sentences.en: So improving their concessions and retail, you know, they get a percentage of all those sales.
sentences.zh: 所以改善特许经营和零售业务，他们能从中抽取一定比例的销售额。

sentences.en: And that's when I realize why there are people like Jim Harding who are paid to do this work.
sentences.zh: 这时我才明白，为什么会有像吉姆·哈丁这样的人，受雇专门做这项工作。

sentences.en: It's not just that airports want us to have a pleasant experience.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是因为机场希望我们有愉快的体验。

sentences.en: It's because there's money on the table.
sentences.zh: 而是因为这背后有实实在在的利益。

sentences.en: Think about it.
sentences.zh: 试想一下。

sentences.en: Say you're trying to make a connecting flight.
sentences.zh: 假设你正在赶转机航班。

sentences.en: You don't have a lot of time.
sentences.zh: 你的时间非常紧迫。

sentences.en: You don't really know where you're going.
sentences.zh: 你根本不知道该往哪走。

sentences.en: If I'm stressed and I don't think I'm going to catch my flight, am I going to take time to open my wallet?
sentences.zh: 如果我感到压力很大，觉得自己赶不上飞机，我还会花时间去掏钱包吗？

sentences.en: Heck no.
sentences.zh: 当然不会。

sentences.en: But if I'm cool, calm, collected, I find my gate, I know where I'm going, I'm more likely to stop and buy whatever.
sentences.zh: 但如果我冷静、从容，找到了登机口，知道自己要去哪，我就更有可能停下来买点什么。

sentences.en: So, you know, that's where wayfinding has a real financial impact, you know, to our airport's bottom line.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是导视系统对机场收益产生实际财务影响的地方。

sentences.en: And so it turns out, wayfinding isn't just about helping you figure out how to get where you want to go.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，导视系统不仅仅是为了帮你找到想去的地方。

sentences.en: It's about steering the masses anywhere that companies hiring the wayfinders want the masses to be steered.
sentences.zh: 它更是为了引导大众前往雇佣导视设计师的公司希望他们去的地方。

sentences.en: And what's more, if your consumer choices aren't going to make money for the powers that be inside of a closed system like an airport,
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，如果你的消费选择不能为机场这种封闭系统内的掌权者带来利润，

sentences.en: don't plan on them making it easy for you.
sentences.zh: 就别指望他们会让你走得顺心。

sentences.en: David Zweig, the writer who introduced me to Jim Harding, he noticed this kind of thing too.
sentences.zh: 大卫·茨威格，那位把我介绍给吉姆·哈丁的作家，也注意到了这一点。

sentences.en: Their job isn't always about creating the best system for us, the traveler.
sentences.zh: 他们的工作并不总是为了给我们这些旅客创造最好的系统。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's who's paying their bills.
sentences.zh: 有时取决于谁在给他们付钱。

sentences.en: When I flew to Florida with my family, we flew into Fort Lauderdale and we foolishly chose an off-site car rental company.
sentences.zh: 我和家人飞往佛罗里达时，降落在劳德代尔堡，我们愚蠢地选择了一家机场外的租车公司。

sentences.en: Ugh, rookies.
sentences.zh: 哎，菜鸟行为。

sentences.en: Yeah, big mistake.
sentences.zh: 没错，大错特错。

sentences.en: We thought like, oh, off-site, it's like you take a shuttle bus, you're there in two minutes.
sentences.zh: 我们当时想，哦，机场外嘛，坐个穿梭巴士，两分钟就到了。

sentences.en: Well, what happened is when you arrive there, there's huge signs for Hertz and Avis and all the companies who are there.
sentences.zh: 结果当你到达那里时，你会看到赫兹、安飞士等所有入驻机场的公司的巨大招牌。

sentences.en: If you're trying to find the off-site car rental companies, good luck.
sentences.zh: 如果你想找机场外的租车公司，祝你好运。

sentences.en: And then if you try doing that with two little kids in tow, oof.
sentences.zh: 如果你还带着两个小孩，那简直是灾难。

sentences.en: David mentioned this to Jim Harding.
sentences.zh: 大卫把这件事告诉了吉姆·哈丁。

sentences.en: I said, Jim, this seems like a wayfinding failure.
sentences.zh: 我说，吉姆，这看起来像是导视系统的失败。

sentences.en: And he said, well, the airport is far more interested in helping out the people who are paying them,
sentences.zh: 他说，机场对帮助那些给他们付钱的人更感兴趣，

sentences.en: who have on-site facilities.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些拥有机场内设施的商家。

sentences.en: They have no incentive to have you leave the airport to go to someone else.
sentences.zh: 他们没有任何动力让你离开机场去别处消费。

sentences.en: They generate no revenue.
sentences.zh: 因为那样他们产生不了任何收入。

sentences.en: Yeah, so they're, you know, it's almost like second-class citizen.
sentences.zh: 没错，所以这几乎就像是二等公民待遇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's not to say, though, that there's necessarily a dichotomy between capitalism and good user experience.
sentences.zh: 不过，这并不是说资本主义与良好的用户体验之间必然存在矛盾。

sentences.en: Why do we do what we do for a living as wayfinders?
sentences.zh: 我们作为导视设计师，为什么以此为生？

sentences.en: And I think it is to, you know, in our own little way, to improve the overall quality of life,
sentences.zh: 我认为这是为了以我们自己的方式，提高整体的生活质量，

sentences.en: that customer experience, passenger experience.
sentences.zh: 改善那种客户体验和乘客体验。

sentences.en: And so you work on a project like the International Terminal here in Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 所以当你参与像亚特兰大国际航站楼这样的项目时，

sentences.en: We work on it for years.
sentences.zh: 我们为此工作了多年。

sentences.en: And after all that time, it's built.
sentences.zh: 经过漫长的等待，它终于建成了。

sentences.en: And you get to walk through it.
sentences.zh: 你有机会走在其中。

sentences.en: You see it like we are today.
sentences.zh: 你像我们今天这样看着它。

sentences.en: You see people using the space, understanding the space.
sentences.zh: 你看到人们在使用这个空间，理解这个空间。

sentences.en: They aren't stressed or freaking out about missing their flight.
sentences.zh: 他们没有因为错过航班而感到压力或惊慌失措。

sentences.en: And it's like, okay, wow, you know, it all works.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得，太棒了，一切都运作良好。

sentences.en: We did a good job.
sentences.zh: 我们做得很好。

sentences.en: And you just come away with a nice sense of satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 你会从中获得一种美好的满足感。

sentences.en: Welcome aboard the plane train.
sentences.zh: 欢迎乘坐机场列车。

sentences.en: Please hold on.
sentences.zh: 请抓好扶手。

sentences.en: This train is departing.
sentences.zh: 列车即将出发。

sentences.en: In theory, wayfinding should work whether you're illiterate in it or not.
sentences.zh: 理论上，无论你是否精通导视系统，它都应该发挥作用。

sentences.en: But learning to see the subtle wayfinding cues in the built landscape can help you understand how you make your decisions.
sentences.zh: 但学会观察建筑环境中微妙的导视线索，可以帮你理解自己是如何做出决策的。

sentences.en: Or it can make you question if you're the one even making your own decisions at all.
sentences.zh: 或者，它会让你怀疑，你是否真的是在自主做出决策。

sentences.en: After I parted ways with Jim Harding, I passed a food court.
sentences.zh: 在与吉姆·哈丁道别后，我经过了一个美食广场。

sentences.en: And I noticed, right outside, in the floor, were these big, black, curvy tiles.
sentences.zh: 我注意到，就在外面的地板上，铺着一些黑色的大型弧形瓷砖。

sentences.en: And they actually seemed to be steering people towards the concessions.
sentences.zh: 它们似乎在引导人们走向特许经营店。

sentences.en: So, you know, next time you find yourself at an airport food court eating a Cinnabon that you didn't even want,
sentences.zh: 所以，下次当你发现自己在机场美食广场吃着一个你根本不想吃的肉桂卷时，

sentences.en: check out the signage, the shape of the tiling, the height of the ceiling, the quality of the light.
sentences.zh: 不妨留意一下导视牌、地砖的形状、天花板的高度和灯光的质量。

sentences.en: It may just be that you have an environmental graphic designer to blame.
sentences.zh: 可能你只能怪罪于某位环境图形设计师了。

sentences.en: But, you know, user error does apply.
sentences.zh: 当然，用户自身的问题也确实存在。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Sam Greenspan with Katie Mingle, Avery Truffleman, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99% Invisible》由萨姆·格林斯潘制作，凯蒂·明格尔、艾弗里·特鲁夫曼和我，罗曼·马斯共同参与。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 Local Public Radio KALW in San Francisco and produced out of the offices of ArcSign,
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山 91.7 本地公共广播电台 KALW 的项目，并在 ArcSign 的办公室制作，

sentences.en: our favorite architecture firm in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 那是我们最喜欢的建筑事务所，位于美丽的加州奥克兰市中心。

sentences.en: You could only listen to these episodes of 99% Invisible and be just fine.
sentences.zh: 你只听这些《99% Invisible》的剧集也完全没问题。

sentences.en: But if you want to be a 12th level 99PI paladin, you should follow us on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想成为 12 级的 99PI 圣骑士，你应该在 Twitter 上关注我们。

sentences.en: We're at Roman Mars, Sam Listens, Katie Mingle, and Truffleman.
sentences.zh: 我们的账号是 Roman Mars, Sam Listens, Katie Mingle 和 Truffleman。

sentences.en: Live show and office hours announcements can be found most reliably on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 现场演出和办公时间的公告最可靠的发布渠道是 Facebook。

sentences.en: We're also all over Tumblr, Instagram, Flickr, SoundCloud, and Spotify too.
sentences.zh: 我们也在 Tumblr、Instagram、Flickr、SoundCloud 和 Spotify 上活跃。

sentences.en: And you're always welcome at our home on the web at 99PI.org.
sentences.zh: 也欢迎随时访问我们的网站 99PI.org。

sentences.en: I'm buying a Cinnabon at the airport that I arrived at.
sentences.zh: 我正在我刚抵达的机场买一个肉桂卷。

sentences.en: You understand why that's extra disgusting, right?
sentences.zh: 你明白为什么这格外令人恶心了吧？

sentences.en: Radiotopia.
sentences.zh: Radiotopia。
